hypothesis: With default TNCA settings on the already-loaded run-1 image, the full-depth official Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct-FP8 checkpoint answers the registered chat-quality prompts (including an image prompt) like the CPU reference model, passes the 2026-10-28 teacher-forced rule, and reproduces a first conversation bit for bit after a second one in the same session.
competing_explanations: a full model exercises an operation that the layer-level and reduced-depth evidence did not cover
a persistent session corrupts state across conversations through code-store reloads, allocator reuse or cache reset
per-image vision calls or chunked prefill behave differently on the board than on the SystemC/TLM model
device execution falls back to host numerical work or recompiles during decode
the loaded image, clock, or shared-card ownership changes during the run
expected_counter_changes: real prefill/decode launches change completion and memory-port traffic counters; the run records the observed deltas without a predetermined traffic or performance target
after the first decode graph is compiled, subsequent decode steps of a prompt add no graphs and perform no host reads
the persistent-session repeat records its graph count, code-store evictions and bitwise logit comparison; a mismatch is recorded as a failure
teacher-forced comparisons, failures and timeouts are recorded rather than assumed to pass
the chat-quality step records every prompt's answer, its scores against the archived CPU answers and its decode rate; a failed score is recorded as a failure
expected_observations: each chat report records the actual prefill/decode calls, graph counts, host transfers, code-store evictions and teacher-forced comparisons
no result is inferred if a step fails or the execution budget expires

tolerance_rule.source: author decision, in the lead's chat, 2026-10-28 (relayed by the coordinator): the per-token logit tolerance may be changed if the new rule is written into the registered spec, with date and justification, before the next result
tolerance_rule.rule: per teacher-forced step: rel_l2(device logits, CPU W8A8 reference logits) <= max(0.05, 2 x the CPU reference's own reciprocal-vs-IEEE scale-rounding floor at that step), and the device argmax equals the reference argmax (chat.py --cpu-floor-multiplier 2 --require-argmax)
tolerance_rule.justification: The CPU W8A8 reference is itself ambiguous at the level of its activation-scale rounding: computing the scale as amax*(1/448) instead of amax/448 moves the Qwen3.5 logits by a relative L2 of 0.05941731822088129 at the second checked token (evidence/r41/chat/q35-cpu-floor-v1.tgz), more than the fixed 0.05 limit. A device that rounds differently but no worse than the reference's own alternatives is within twice that floor; the argmax requirement keeps the chosen token itself exact. The 0.05 minimum keeps the old limit wherever the floor is small.
tolerance_rule.prior_results: Runs before this registration are judged by the fixed 0.05 rule and keep their judgments (the Qwen3.5 TLM runs remain failed).

chat_quality.source: author decision, in the lead's chat, 2026-10-28: the acceptance criterion is whether the final model can hold a normal conversation and show normal intelligence; a registered chat-quality check fixed before the run
chat_quality.prefill: text turns are prefilled in chunks of 8 tokens with the remainder through the decode graph, so the compiled prefill shapes stay bounded across prompts; image turns are prefilled whole; graphs compile with static shapes

environment.status: author-approved as the default chat environment, in the lead's chat, 2026-10-28

budget_note: The queue's 10,800-second execution cap applies across the steps in order; a step that does not fit is recorded as not run or stopped.
